item.title: 13 Pseudocode

item.title: 04 - Euler's Method in Pseudocode
item.description: Euler’s Method in Pseudocode Euler’s Method is a method for approximating solutions to differential equations of the form \dfrac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y).

item.title: 03 - Functions and Lists
item.description: Functions and Lists Functions The Euclidean Algorithm to find the highest common factor is an example of a function; it requires one or more inputs to return an output.

item.description: Pseudocode — Iteration and Selection Pseudocode is a way of writing algorithms without using a programming language; instead it uses Structured English.

item.title: 01 - Algorithms
item.description: Algorithms What are Algorithms? An algorithm is a step-by-step process that produces a desired outcome or performs a specific task.

item.title: 06 - Type I and Type II Errors
item.description: Errors in Hypothesis Testing Key Ideas In hypothesis testing, two types of errors can occur: Type I error: Rejecting H_0 when it is actually true (false positive).

item.title: 05 - Hypothesis Testing
item.description: Hypothesis Testing Key Ideas Hypothesis testing is a procedure for testing a claim about a population parameter.

item.title: 04 - Confidence Intervals
item.description: Confidence Intervals Key Ideas A point estimate is a single value used to estimate a population parameter (e.g., \bar{x} estimates \mu).
